Introduction

Our group chose to focus on examining how Sam’s Club can maximize their profit by filtering between store sizes and their geographical location to see how sales, number of items sold, and number of items returned impacts revenue. Sam’s Club is a direct rival to Costco, and CEO Chris Nicholas is aware of the influence and control the leaders in the wholesale industry have. In an interview with Yahoo Finance, he cited their main path to growth and competing with Costco is retention of and acquiring more memberships. We looked to see if there were alternative paths they could follow to grow their yearly profit. We used the following question to guide our research: How should Sam’s Club tailor product assortment and inventory allocation across regions and store sizes to increase sales productivity and reduce slow-moving or high-return merchandise?

For our analysis, we defined small stores as any below 130,000 square feet, large as any above 140,000 square feet, and medium as the any store between those dimensions. We used the following image as a guideline for creating our four regions: North, South, Midwest, and West.

Map of Regions

Average Item Quantity by Region and Store Size

SQL Query

SELECT CASE
  WHEN i.STATE IN ('ME', 'NH', 'VT', 'MA', 'RI', 'CT', 'NY', 'NJ', 'PA') THEN 'Northeast'
  WHEN i.STATE IN ('DE', 'MD', 'DC', 'VA', 'WV', 'KY', 'NC', 'SC', 'TN', 'GA', 'FL', 'AL', 'MS', 'LA', 'AR', 'TX', 'OK', 'PR') THEN 'South'
  WHEN i.STATE IN ('OH', 'MI', 'IN', 'IL', 'WI', 'MN', 'IA', 'MO', 'KS', 'NE', 'SD', 'ND') THEN 'Midwest'
  WHEN i.STATE IN ('MT', 'WY', 'CO', 'NM', 'AZ', 'UT', 'ID', 'WA', 'OR', 'NV', 'CA', 'AK', 'HI') THEN 'West'
  END AS region,
CASE
  WHEN i.SIZE_SQFT < 130000 THEN 'Small'
  WHEN i.SIZE_SQFT <= 140000 THEN 'Medium'
  ELSE 'Large'
  END AS store_size,
AVG(v.TOT_SCAN_CNT) AS item_quantity
FROM "WCOB_SAMS_INTEGRATED"."VISIT" AS v
JOIN "WCOB_SAMS_INTEGRATED"."STORE_INFO" AS i ON v.STORE_NBR = i.STORE_NBR
GROUP BY region, store_size
ORDER BY region, store_size;

Visualization

## Warning: package 'ggplot2' was built under R version 4.5.2

There is a modest difference in average item quantity across regions. The Northeast has the highest average item quantity with the Midwest close behind. The South and West have the lowest average item quantity. Across most regions, excluding the Midwest, small stores had the highest average item quantity. Medium stores had the least across all regions.

SQL Query for Regression

SELECT CASE
  WHEN i.STATE IN ('ME', 'NH', 'VT', 'MA', 'RI', 'CT', 'NY', 'NJ', 'PA') THEN 'Northeast'
  WHEN i.STATE IN ('DE', 'MD', 'DC', 'VA', 'WV', 'KY', 'NC', 'SC', 'TN', 'GA', 'FL', 'AL', 'MS', 'LA', 'AR', 'TX', 'OK', 'PR') THEN 'South'
  WHEN i.STATE IN ('OH', 'MI', 'IN', 'IL', 'WI', 'MN', 'IA', 'MO', 'KS', 'NE', 'SD', 'ND') THEN 'Midwest'
  WHEN i.STATE IN ('MT', 'WY', 'CO', 'NM', 'AZ', 'UT', 'ID', 'WA', 'OR', 'NV', 'CA', 'AK', 'HI') THEN 'West'
  END AS region,
CASE
  WHEN i.SIZE_SQFT < 130000 THEN 'Small'
  WHEN i.SIZE_SQFT <= 140000 THEN 'Medium'
  ELSE 'Large'
  END AS store_size,
v.TOT_SCAN_CNT
FROM "WCOB_SAMS_INTEGRATED"."VISIT" AS v
JOIN "WCOB_SAMS_INTEGRATED"."STORE_INFO" AS i ON v.STORE_NBR = i.STORE_NBR
WHERE v.TOT_SCAN_CNT > 0 AND v.TOT_VISIT_AMT > 0;

Statistical Analysis

## 
## Call:
## glm.nb(formula = TOT_SCAN_CNT ~ region + store_size, data = reg_sample, 
##     init.theta = 0.9612467345, link = log)
## 
## Coefficients:
##                  Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)    
## (Intercept)       1.84251    0.01704 108.100  < 2e-16 ***
## regionNortheast   0.12334    0.01984   6.217 5.07e-10 ***
## regionSouth      -0.04935    0.01218  -4.051 5.09e-05 ***
## regionWest       -0.06148    0.01572  -3.911 9.19e-05 ***
## store_sizeMedium -0.04195    0.01576  -2.662  0.00776 ** 
## store_sizeSmall   0.04479    0.01886   2.375  0.01754 *  
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 
## (Dispersion parameter for Negative Binomial(0.9612) family taken to be 1)
## 
##     Null deviance: 52086  on 49999  degrees of freedom
## Residual deviance: 51935  on 49994  degrees of freedom
## AIC: 287332
## 
## Number of Fisher Scoring iterations: 1
## 
## 
##               Theta:  0.96125 
##           Std. Err.:  0.00649 
## 
##  2 x log-likelihood:  -287317.57500

A negative binomial regression was conducted to evaluate the effects of geographic region and store size on item quantity.

\(H_{0}: (\beta_{region},\: \beta_{store\: size}) = 0\)

\(H_{a}: At\: least\: one\: of\: (\beta_{region},\: \beta_{store\: size}) \neq 0\)

The results indicate that both region and store size have statistically significant effects on a customer’s item quantity (p-value < 0.05). Therefore, we reject the null hypothesis and conclude that at least one of these variables influences how many items a customer purchases. Additionally, the significance of each predictor suggests that both factors contribute to explaining variation in item quantity.

The findings also suggest that while the quantity of items a customer purchases is influenced by region and store size, these variables explain only a limited portion of the variation.

Top Selling Items by Region and Store Size

SQL Query

SELECT CASE
  WHEN i.STATE IN ('ME', 'NH', 'VT', 'MA', 'RI', 'CT', 'NY', 'NJ', 'PA') THEN 'Northeast'
  WHEN i.STATE IN ('DE', 'MD', 'DC', 'VA', 'WV', 'KY', 'NC', 'SC', 'TN', 'GA', 'FL', 'AL', 'MS', 'LA', 'AR', 'TX', 'OK', 'PR') THEN 'South'
  WHEN i.STATE IN ('OH', 'MI', 'IN', 'IL', 'WI', 'MN', 'IA', 'MO', 'KS', 'NE', 'SD', 'ND') THEN 'Midwest'
  WHEN i.STATE IN ('MT', 'WY', 'CO', 'NM', 'AZ', 'UT', 'ID', 'WA', 'OR', 'NV', 'CA', 'AK', 'HI') THEN 'West'
  END AS region,
CASE
  WHEN i.SIZE_SQFT < 130000 THEN 'Small'
  WHEN i.SIZE_SQFT <= 140000 THEN 'Medium'
  ELSE 'Large'
  END AS store_size,
d.Primary_Desc AS item, SUM(s.unit_qty * s.retail_price) AS revenue
FROM "WCOB_SAMS_INTEGRATED"."ITEM_SCAN" AS s
JOIN "WCOB_SAMS_INTEGRATED"."ITEM_DESC" AS d ON s.SCAN_ID = d.Item_Nbr
JOIN "WCOB_SAMS_INTEGRATED"."STORE_INFO" AS i ON s.STORE_NBR = i.STORE_NBR
WHERE s.SCAN_TYPE = 0
GROUP BY region, store_size, item
QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER
(PARTITION BY region, store_size
ORDER BY SUM(s.unit_qty * s.retail_price) DESC) <= 5;

Items Frequently Bought Together

SQL Query

SELECT d1.Primary_Desc AS item_1, d2.Primary_Desc AS item_2, COUNT(*) AS times_bought_together
FROM "WCOB_SAMS_INTEGRATED"."ITEM_SCAN" AS s1
JOIN "WCOB_SAMS_INTEGRATED"."ITEM_SCAN" AS s2 ON s1.VISIT_NBR = s2.VISIT_NBR AND s1.STORE_NBR = s2.STORE_NBR AND s1.SCAN_ID < s2.SCAN_ID
JOIN "WCOB_SAMS_INTEGRATED"."ITEM_DESC" AS d1 ON s1.SCAN_TYPE = 0 AND s1.SCAN_ID = d1.ITEM_NBR
JOIN "WCOB_SAMS_INTEGRATED"."ITEM_DESC" AS d2 ON s2.SCAN_TYPE = 0 AND s2.SCAN_ID = d2.ITEM_NBR
WHERE s1.RETURNED_ITEM_IND = 0 AND s2.RETURNED_ITEM_IND = 0 AND d1.Primary_Desc NOT LIKE '%OFF%' AND d2.Primary_Desc NOT LIKE '%OFF%'
GROUP BY item_1, item_2
QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC) <= 10;

Visualization

There are many items that are commonly bought together at Sam’s Club, the most frequent being grocery staples.

Bundle vs. No Bundle Example (milk and bananas)

SQL Query

SELECT CASE
WHEN bananas = 1 AND milk = 1 THEN 'Bundle'
ELSE 'No bundle'
END AS bundle_check,
AVG(TOT_VISIT_AMT) AS avg_spend, COUNT(*) AS total_transactions
FROM (
SELECT
v.VISIT_NBR, v.STORE_NBR, v.TOT_VISIT_AMT,
MAX(CASE WHEN d.Primary_Desc = 'BANANAS' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS bananas,
MAX(CASE WHEN d.Primary_Desc = '2% MILK' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS milk
FROM "WCOB_SAMS_INTEGRATED"."VISIT" AS v
JOIN "WCOB_SAMS_INTEGRATED"."ITEM_SCAN" AS s ON v.VISIT_NBR = s.VISIT_NBR AND v.STORE_NBR = s.STORE_NBR
JOIN "WCOB_SAMS_INTEGRATED"."ITEM_DESC" AS d ON s.SCAN_TYPE = 0 AND s.SCAN_ID = d.ITEM_NBR
WHERE v.TOT_VISIT_AMT > 0
GROUP BY v.VISIT_NBR, v.STORE_NBR, v.TOT_VISIT_AMT
) AS x
GROUP BY CASE
WHEN bananas = 1 AND milk = 1
THEN 'Bundle'
ELSE 'No bundle'
END;

Total Returns by Region and Store Size

SQL Query

SELECT CASE
  WHEN i.STATE IN ('ME', 'NH', 'VT', 'MA', 'RI', 'CT', 'NY', 'NJ', 'PA') THEN 'Northeast'
  WHEN i.STATE IN ('DE', 'MD', 'DC', 'VA', 'WV', 'KY', 'NC', 'SC', 'TN', 'GA', 'FL', 'AL', 'MS', 'LA', 'AR', 'TX', 'OK', 'PR') THEN 'South'
  WHEN i.STATE IN ('OH', 'MI', 'IN', 'IL', 'WI', 'MN', 'IA', 'MO', 'KS', 'NE', 'SD', 'ND') THEN 'Midwest'
  WHEN i.STATE IN ('MT', 'WY', 'CO', 'NM', 'AZ', 'UT', 'ID', 'WA', 'OR', 'NV', 'CA', 'AK', 'HI') THEN 'West'
  END AS region,
CASE
  WHEN i.SIZE_SQFT < 130000 THEN 'Small'
  WHEN i.SIZE_SQFT <= 140000 THEN 'Medium'
  ELSE 'Large'
  END AS store_size,
count(s.RETURNED_ITEM_IND ) AS return_total
FROM "WCOB_SAMS_INTEGRATED"."ITEM_SCAN" AS S
JOIN "WCOB_SAMS_INTEGRATED"."STORE_INFO" AS I ON S.STORE_NBR = I.STORE_NBR
GROUP BY region, store_size
ORDER BY region, store_size;

Visualization

The graphs show the South region has the most number of returns total. Grouped by store size, medium stores see the most total returns.

Statistical Analysis

## 
## Call:
## lm(formula = return_total ~ region + store_size, data = tot_return)
## 
## Residuals:
##       Min        1Q    Median        3Q       Max 
## -60677510 -29864434   4467658  26190266  87480911 
## 
## Coefficients:
##                   Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)  
## (Intercept)       27764804   40165225   0.691   0.5152  
## regionNortheast  -51406660   46378806  -1.108   0.3101  
## regionSouth       79890955   46378806   1.723   0.1357  
## regionWest       -29426909   46378806  -0.634   0.5492  
## store_sizeMedium 141904374   40165225   3.533   0.0123 *
## store_sizeSmall   16641822   40165225   0.414   0.6930  
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 
## Residual standard error: 56800000 on 6 degrees of freedom
## Multiple R-squared:  0.8008, Adjusted R-squared:  0.6348 
## F-statistic: 4.823 on 5 and 6 DF,  p-value: 0.04074
##         1         2         3         4         5         6         7         8 
##  27764804 169669178  44406626 -23641856 118262518  -7000034 107655759 249560133 
##         9        10        11        12 
## 124297581  -1662105 140242269  14979717
##                       2.5 %    97.5 %
## (Intercept)       -70515960 126045568
## regionNortheast  -164891511  62078191

\(H_{0}: \beta_{region} = \beta_{store size}\)

\(H_{a}\): at least one of \((\beta_{region}, \beta_{store size})\) is not equal to zero

Based on the p-value of 0.04074, we can conclude that at least one variable is statistically significant and has an impact on the rate of returns at Sam’s Club. We reject the null hypothesis and determine that store size or the region has an impact on how frequently customers are making returns. Looking at the variables p-values, we can see the Medium store size has a p-value of 0.0123, and therefore we can conclude the medium store size has a greater impact on the rate of returns.

Average Returns by Region and Store Size

SQL Query

SELECT CASE
  WHEN i.STATE IN ('ME', 'NH', 'VT', 'MA', 'RI', 'CT', 'NY', 'NJ', 'PA') THEN 'Northeast'
  WHEN i.STATE IN ('DE', 'MD', 'DC', 'VA', 'WV', 'KY', 'NC', 'SC', 'TN', 'GA', 'FL', 'AL', 'MS', 'LA', 'AR', 'TX', 'OK', 'PR') THEN 'South'
  WHEN i.STATE IN ('OH', 'MI', 'IN', 'IL', 'WI', 'MN', 'IA', 'MO', 'KS', 'NE', 'SD', 'ND') THEN 'Midwest'
  WHEN i.STATE IN ('MT', 'WY', 'CO', 'NM', 'AZ', 'UT', 'ID', 'WA', 'OR', 'NV', 'CA', 'AK', 'HI') THEN 'West'
  END AS region,
CASE
  WHEN i.SIZE_SQFT < 130000 THEN 'Small'
  WHEN i.SIZE_SQFT <= 140000 THEN 'Medium'
  ELSE 'Large'
  END AS store_size,
AVG(s.RETURNED_ITEM_IND ) AS return_average
FROM "WCOB_SAMS_INTEGRATED"."ITEM_SCAN" AS S
JOIN "WCOB_SAMS_INTEGRATED"."STORE_INFO" AS I ON S.STORE_NBR = I.STORE_NBR
GROUP BY region, store_size
ORDER BY region, store_size;

Visualization

These graphs show that on average, Midwest stores see more returns per transaction than any other region. It also shows that medium sized stores have more returns on average than any other store size in every region except for the Northeast.

Total Sales by Region and Store Size

SQL Query

region_store_size_summary:

WITH store_classification AS (
    SELECT
        STORE_NBR,
        STATE,
        SIZE_SQFT,
        CASE
            WHEN SIZE_SQFT < 130000 THEN 'Small'
            WHEN SIZE_SQFT BETWEEN 130000 AND 140000 THEN 'Medium'
            ELSE 'Large'
        END AS store_size,
        CASE
            WHEN STATE IN ('CA','OR','WA','NV','AZ','UT','ID','MT','WY','CO','NM','AK','HI') THEN 'West'
            WHEN STATE IN ('ND','SD','NE','KS','MN','IA','MO','WI','IL','IN','MI','OH') THEN 'Midwest'
            WHEN STATE IN ('TX','OK','AR','LA','MS','AL','GA','FL','SC','NC','TN','KY','WV','VA','MD','DC','DE') THEN 'South'
            WHEN STATE IN ('ME','NH','VT','MA','RI','CT','NY','PA','NJ') THEN 'Northeast'
            ELSE 'Other'
        END AS region
    FROM WCOB_SAMS_INTEGRATED.STORE_INFO
)

SELECT
    sc.region,
    sc.store_size,
    COUNT(DISTINCT v.STORE_NBR) AS num_stores,
    COUNT(*) AS num_visits,
    SUM(v.TOT_VISIT_AMT) AS total_sales,
    AVG(v.TOT_VISIT_AMT) AS avg_spend_per_visit
FROM WCOB_SAMS_INTEGRATED.VISIT v
JOIN store_classification sc
    ON v.STORE_NBR = sc.STORE_NBR
GROUP BY sc.region, sc.store_size
ORDER BY sc.region, sc.store_size;

visit_spending_anova:

WITH store_classification AS (
    SELECT
        STORE_NBR,
        STATE,
        SIZE_SQFT,
        CASE
            WHEN SIZE_SQFT < 130000 THEN 'Small'
            WHEN SIZE_SQFT BETWEEN 130000 AND 140000 THEN 'Medium'
            ELSE 'Large'
        END AS store_size,
        CASE
            WHEN STATE IN ('CA','OR','WA','NV','AZ','UT','ID','MT','WY','CO','NM','AK','HI') THEN 'West'
            WHEN STATE IN ('ND','SD','NE','KS','MN','IA','MO','WI','IL','IN','MI','OH') THEN 'Midwest'
            WHEN STATE IN ('TX','OK','AR','LA','MS','AL','GA','FL','SC','NC','TN','KY','WV','VA','MD','DC','DE') THEN 'South'
            WHEN STATE IN ('ME','NH','VT','MA','RI','CT','NY','PA','NJ') THEN 'Northeast'
            ELSE 'Other'
        END AS region
    FROM WCOB_SAMS_INTEGRATED.STORE_INFO
)

SELECT
    v.TOT_VISIT_AMT,
    sc.region,
    sc.store_size
FROM WCOB_SAMS_INTEGRATED.VISIT v
JOIN store_classification sc
    ON v.STORE_NBR = sc.STORE_NBR
WHERE sc.region <> 'Other';

Visualization

Statistical Analysis

A two-way ANOVA was used to test whether customer spending differs by region, store size, and their interaction.

  • \(H_0^{(1)}\): Store size has no effect on spending
  • \(H_0^{(2)}\): Region has no effect on spending
  • \(H_0^{(3)}\): There is no interaction between store size and region
##                        Df    Sum Sq Mean Sq F value   Pr(>F)    
## region                  3 3.720e+06 1240012  11.588 1.37e-07 ***
## store_size              2 5.603e+06 2801592  26.182 4.26e-12 ***
## region:store_size       6 5.052e+06  842040   7.869 1.70e-08 ***
## Residuals         1048563 1.122e+11  107004                     
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1

A two-way ANOVA was conducted to evaluate the effects of store size and geographic region on customer spending (measured by total visit amount).

The results indicate that both region (F = 159.25, p < 0.001) and store size (F = 240.76, p < 0.001) have statistically significant effects on customer spending. Therefore, we reject the null hypotheses \(H_0^{(1)}\) and \(H_0^{(2)}\), concluding that both store size and region influence customer spending.

Additionally, the interaction between region and store size was also significant (F = 77.44, p < 0.001). Thus, we reject the null hypothesis \(H_0^{(3)}\), indicating that the effect of store size on spending varies across regions.

These findings suggest that customer spending behavior is influenced not only by store size and location independently, but also by the interaction between these factors.

Boxplot

The boxplot further supports the ANOVA results by showing variation in spending distributions across regions and store sizes.

Summary Results

SQL Query

SELECT 
  CASE
    WHEN i.STATE IN ('ME', 'NH', 'VT', 'MA', 'RI', 'CT', 'NY', 'NJ', 'PA') THEN 'Northeast'
    WHEN i.STATE IN ('DE', 'MD', 'DC', 'VA', 'WV', 'KY', 'NC', 'SC', 'TN', 'GA', 'FL', 'AL', 'MS', 'LA', 'AR', 'TX', 'OK', 'PR') THEN 'South'
    WHEN i.STATE IN ('OH', 'MI', 'IN', 'IL', 'WI', 'MN', 'IA', 'MO', 'KS', 'NE', 'SD', 'ND') THEN 'Midwest'
    WHEN i.STATE IN ('MT', 'WY', 'CO', 'NM', 'AZ', 'UT', 'ID', 'WA', 'OR', 'NV', 'CA', 'AK', 'HI') THEN 'West'
  END AS region,
  CASE
    WHEN i.SIZE_SQFT < 130000 THEN 'Small'
    WHEN i.SIZE_SQFT <= 140000 THEN 'Medium'
    ELSE 'Large'
  END AS store_size,
  COUNT(DISTINCT i.STORE_NBR) AS num_stores, 
COUNT(DISTINCT v.VISIT_NBR) AS num_visits, 
AVG(CAST(v.TOT_VISIT_AMT AS FLOAT)) AS avg_spend_per_visit, 
AVG(CAST(v.TOT_SCAN_CNT AS FLOAT)) AS avg_items, 
AVG(CAST(s.RETURNED_ITEM_IND AS FLOAT)) AS average_returns
FROM "WCOB_SAMS_INTEGRATED"."STORE_INFO" AS i
JOIN "WCOB_SAMS_INTEGRATED"."VISIT" AS v 
  ON i.STORE_NBR = v.STORE_NBR
JOIN "WCOB_SAMS_INTEGRATED"."ITEM_SCAN" AS s 
  ON v.VISIT_NBR = s.VISIT_NBR 
  AND v.STORE_NBR = s.STORE_NBR
GROUP BY region, store_size
ORDER BY region, store_size;

Table

Conclusion

Through our research, we were able to make several conclusions. First, average item quantity for both large and small stores is higher than that of medium stores across all of the regions. While medium stores have the lowest average item quantity per customer, they also have the highest total number of returns and consistently the highest amount of returns on average.

Inversely, medium stores had the highest total sales across all regions. Though, their average spend was lower than small and large stores.

Out of the 4 regions, the South had the highest total sales.

Looking at data of top-selling items, we see that it is mostly consistent across regions and store sizes. These are primarily essentials goods like groceries, fuel, and certain household items.

And looking at data of items that are frequently bought together, we see that transactions with certain pairs have an average higher spend per customer overall. There are opportunities for Sam’s Club to bundle items to improve their sales productivity and improve turnover of slow-moving or higher-margin merchandise. These bundle promotions could be put on end caps or displays near the top-performing items locations.

Sam’s Club can use the region-specific data of top-performing products and products that are frequently bought together to tailor their bundling to align with more localized customer behavior. In doing so, we believe that Sam’s Club can increase their sales productivity and operational efficiency.
